Create an environment from a file

Source: R/env_definition.R
env_definition.Rd

Marks a file as the definition of a Conda environment, such as an environment YAML file or a lock file. Pass the result in the ... of create_env(), in place of package specs: create_env(env_definition("environment.yml"), env_name = "tools"). install_packages() and validate_env() take it too (see Other functions).

Usage

env_definition(path, format = NULL, ...)

Arguments

path

Character string with the path of the file, absolute or relative to the working directory. env_definition() expands a leading ~. A backend may also accept a directory. URLs are not supported: download the file first. A value that is not a single, non-empty string, or a URL, aborts with class condathis_env_definition_invalid_path (also condathis_invalid_path).

format

NULL (the default), so that the backend detects the format, or a single, non-empty string that names it (see Formats). Other values abort with class condathis_env_definition_invalid_format.

...

Named options for the backend, such as categories for a conda-lock file. condathis passes them on and never reads them. An unnamed or repeated option aborts with class condathis_env_definition_invalid_options.

Value

An object of class condathis_env_definition: a list with path (the absolute path), format (NULL or a string) and options (a named list).

Details

condathis does not read the file. The backend reads it and tells condathis two things: which format the file has, and whether it is a request or a lock.

  • A request, such as an environment YAML file or a list of package specs, is solved when the environment is created. The result depends on the channels and on the day.

  • A lock, such as an @EXPLICIT file or a conda-lock file, lists exact packages. It is installed as it is, without a solve, and only for a platform it lists.

env_definition() makes path absolute against the working directory at the time of the call, so a later setwd() does not change which file it refers to. It does not resolve symbolic links, so paths in the file that are relative to the file, such as -r requirements.txt in a pip: section, still resolve. create_env() checks that the file exists when it runs.

Formats

Leave format as NULL and the backend detects the format. Give it when the file name does not tell, for example for a lock file named ci.lock. condathis passes format to the backend and never reads it. These names are a convention: conda uses them for its --format option. Backends should accept them:

  • "environment-yaml" (also "cep-24"): an environment YAML file, with channels: and dependencies:. A request.

  • "requirements": a text file with one package spec per line. A request.

  • "explicit": an @EXPLICIT file, with one package URL per line. A lock.

  • "conda-lock-v1": a conda-lock file, version 1. A lock.

  • "rattler-lock-v6" and "rattler-lock-v7" (also "pixi"): a pixi.lock file. A lock.

  • "mambajs-lock-v1": a lock file of mambajs, in JSON. A lock.

The micromamba backend reads environment YAML, requirements, @EXPLICIT, conda-lock version 1 and mambajs files. It detects the format from the contents of the file, so the file can have any name, with one exception: an environment YAML file must have a name that ends in .yml or .yaml, and not in -lock.yml or -lock.yaml. It does not read pixi.lock files or directories. For a conda-lock file, it accepts one option, categories: the package categories to install, "main" by default, as in categories = c("main", "dev"). A backend aborts for an option it does not know.

Locks

For a lock, create_env() picks the platform from the platforms that the file lists: platform when it is given, else the native platform of the backend, else an emulated one (see platform in create_env()). When the file lists none of these, create_env() aborts with class condathis_create_env_platform_not_locked (also condathis_create_env_platform_mismatch) before anything runs. A lock of noarch packages lists no platform, and installs on any platform. For an @EXPLICIT or mambajs file, micromamba takes the platform of each package from its subdir, such as noarch or linux-64, not from the platform header of the file. channels, additional_channels and channel_priority cannot be given with a lock: a lock names its packages by URL. They abort with class condathis_create_env_conflicting_args. The deprecated env_file argument of create_env() ignores them, as in 0.1.4. A lock that lists packages but gives an empty environment aborts with class condathis_create_env_failed.

When the backend reports the packages of a lock, as micromamba does for @EXPLICIT, conda-lock and mambajs files, an existing environment is compared with them: the same names, versions and build strings, none missing and none more, for the platform of the lock. Packages that pip installed are left out. create_env(overwrite = FALSE) then keeps an environment that has exactly those packages, and validate_env(env_definition(<lock>), env_name = ...) returns TRUE.

Other functions

  • install_packages() installs the packages of a request into an existing environment, as micromamba install -f <file> does. It aborts for a lock, with class condathis_install_packages_unsupported_definition: create the environment again with create_env(..., overwrite = TRUE).

  • validate_env() compares an environment with a lock (see Locks). It aborts for a request, with class condathis_validate_env_unsupported_definition: a request depends on the channels and on the day.

  • With method = "auto", create_env() creates a new environment with the first available backend in condathis.backend_priority order that does not say it cannot read the file. An explicit method, or an existing environment, keeps its backend.

See also

create_env()

Other environments: create_env(), env_exists(), env_path(), get_env_dir(), install_packages(), list_envs(), list_packages(), remove_env(), validate_env()

Examples

condathis::env_definition("environment.yml")
#> <env_definition> /home/runner/work/condathis/condathis/docs/reference/environment.yml
condathis::env_definition("ci.lock", format = "conda-lock-v1")
#> <env_definition> /home/runner/work/condathis/condathis/docs/reference/ci.lock (format: conda-lock-v1)
condathis::env_definition("conda-lock.yml", categories = c("main", "dev"))
#> <env_definition> /home/runner/work/condathis/condathis/docs/reference/conda-lock.yml (options: categories)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # An environment YAML file shipped with condathis.
  env_file <- system.file("extdata", "stat-env.yml", package = "condathis")
  condathis::create_env(
    condathis::env_definition(env_file),
    env_name = "stat-env"
  )
})
} # }
